description:
FILED s473s (2026-09-08) from the own-class method cache's invalidation probes
(the cache is NOT the cause -- measured on the runtime BEFORE it, commit
0c90e681, which answers the same).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s473s/pr-inval.pl rows 5-6, minimised):

    package Base; sub new { bless {}, $_[0] } sub m1 { "Base::m1" }
    package Kid;  our @ISA = ('Base'); sub m1 { "Kid::m1" }
    package main;
    my $k = Kid->new;
    print $k->m1, "\n";                       # Kid::m1  (both)
    { no strict 'refs'; undef &Kid::m1; }
    my $r = eval { $k->m1 };
    print defined $r ? $r : "ERR:$@";

    perl 5.40.3:  ERR:Undefined subroutine called at - line N.
    PCL:          Base::m1

WHY.  perl's `undef &Foo::bar` empties the CV's body but leaves the CV in the
glob's CODE slot, so method resolution FINDS Kid::m1 and then dies calling it.
PCL's implementation `fmakunbound`s the symbol (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the
`undef &NAME` arm), which is indistinguishable from "the class never had that
method" -- so the @ISA walk continues and the parent's method answers.

The same difference shows for a plain call: `undef &f; f()` dies "Undefined
subroutine &main::f called" in perl; PCL's answer was not measured here.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not designed): the glob's CODE slot needs a third state
between "no symbol" and "fbound" -- e.g. binding the symbol to a stub that
dies with perl's message, with `%pcl-own-method-symbol`'s `fboundp` test
(and `can`, and the @ISA walk) treating that stub as PRESENT.  That is a
change to the sub-existence model, not a one-liner: `defined &Foo::bar`,
`Foo->can('bar')` and `exists $Foo::{bar}` must all keep answering what perl
says afterwards, and perl's own answers for the four of them differ.

Guarded as a CANARY in Pl/t/method-cache-01.t row 1 (it asserts PCL's current
"Base::m1" with this task number beside it): when this is fixed that row fails
and its expectation becomes perl's "ERR:undef-sub".
subject: `undef &Foo::bar` REMOVES the sub in PCL, so the next `$obj->bar` INHERITS the parent's method; perl empties the CV but leaves it in the glob, so the call dies "Undefined subroutine called" (PRE-EXISTING, measured on the pre-cache runtime; found by s473s's method-cache invalidation probes)
